inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares, FY2026 Annual Report note 4.1 (1,230.5m; basic 1,230.3m). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows (A$86m, 0.12% of revenue) and the DRP is immaterial to the count (1,228-1,230m over FY2022-FY2026). No buyback since the A$2.0bn FY2022 off-market buyback funded by the Endeavour demerger.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report, statement of changes in equity / note 2.3 'Share-based payments expense' A$86m (FY2025 A$80m). No separate equity-award tax line; employee-trust share purchases (A$85m FY2026) are the cash settlement of the same awards and are not added on top.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 28 June (52/53-week year ending last Sunday of June)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-denominated flows discounted at an AUD-built WACC of 7.5%: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.4%, equity risk premium 5.0%, equity beta ~0.65 for a defensive duopoly grocer gives a cost of equity ~7.7%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (A$5.2bn borrowings, BBB+/Baa1, ~5.0% pre-tax at 30%) on ~7% debt weight ex leases. Leases are charged in the flows (treatment B), so lease liabilities are not in the capital structure. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the driver paths and the probability weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) - leases as operating cost. The full lease cash payment (FY2026: A$1,298m principal, financing activities, note 3.5.2 + A$586m interest, operating activities = A$1,884m, 2.63% of revenue) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (A$11,316m at 28 Jun 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the tax line is ex right-of-use depreciation: total D&A A$2,984m less 'Depreciation - lease assets' A$1,229m (note 2.3.3) = A$1,755m, 2.45% of revenue. Underlying EBIT reported post-AASB 16 (A$3,105m) restates to ~A$2,450m on this cash-lease basis; 30% tax on that is A$735m against A$728m cash tax actually paid in FY2026, so the FY0 build ties.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); non-controlling interests (A$115m book, FY2026 note 5.2.3; A$14m profit share) are deducted once in the equity bridge. Not folded into the flows as well.
inputs.ebitda_basis_note: ebitda_margin_path is pre-SBC, post-AASB 16, before significant items. FY2026 anchor: underlying EBITDA A$6,089m (which is already after the A$86m SBC expense) + A$86m = A$6,175m = 8.63% of revenue; the engine then deducts sbc_pct_path so SBC is charged exactly once. Significant items excluded from the operating margin: FY2026 A$698m pre-tax (A$710m payroll remediation + A$20m interest, less small credits), FY2025 A$569m, FY2024 A$1,607m (A$1,492m NZ Food goodwill impairment, non-cash). The remediation cash is captured through the equity bridge instead.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US, material leases -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md sections a1, b, c, f). Fresh build, no prior DCF and no memory entry. Woolworths is a scale food retailer whose value is a stream of free cash flow, so the default engine applies; the adaptations that matter are AASB 16 leases (treatment B, see lease_treatment), an AUD-built WACC, and NCI charged once. BASE PERIOD: FY2022 onward is the clean post-Endeavour-demerger series (Endeavour Group demerged 30 June 2021; FY2021 is continuing-ops only, FY2020 and earlier include Endeavour). FY2016-FY2021 history is context only and is not used for growth or margin anchoring. OWNER FCF: last_fcf = reported FCF (OCF 4,948 - capex 2,435 = 2,513, with lease interest already inside OCF) - lease principal 1,298 - SBC 86 = A$1,129m. Interest income (A$32m) is NOT stripped: the company is net debt (A$3.7bn ex leases), so there is no cash pile being double-counted. last_fcf is a levered figure (after ~A$236m net non-lease interest paid); the unlevered component build for FY2027 lands ~A$1.3bn, consistent after the ~A$165m post-tax interest add-back. HISTORICAL OWNER FCF on the same basis: FY2022 -196, FY2023 1,055, FY2024 581, FY2025 719, FY2026 1,129 - cash dividends (A$1.0-1.7bn/yr) have exceeded owner FCF in most years and net borrowings rose from A$3.8bn (FY2023) to A$5.2bn (FY2026); the dividend is partly debt-funded on this basis. BUYBACKS: none since FY2022; the flat share count is a convention funded by SBC being immaterial (0.12%), not by repurchases. WORKING CAPITAL: grocers run negative working capital (payables > inventory + receivables), so growth releases cash; wc_capture_pct is positive but modest (3%) and applied to the revenue CHANGE. CAPEX: FY2026 A$2,435m (3.40%) after FY2024-25 A$2.5bn peaks with the Moorebank RDC build (opened Nov-2025); glides to 3.0% as supply-chain renewal rolls off, still ~0.45pp above ex-ROU D&A at maturity for store renewals and new stores.

equity_bridge.note: Company net debt ex leases is A$3,753m 'including derivatives' vs A$3,664m borrowings less cash; FY2026 Annual Report p.2562.
FY2026 note 5.2.3; flows are 100% consolidated so NCI is deducted once here.

equity_bridge.item: Team member remediation provision, post-tax cash still to be paid
equity_bridge.note: A$850m pre-tax provision at 28 June 2026 (note 3.12.1; FY2025 A$146m), tax-deductible at 30% = ~A$595m. Excluded from the operating flows as a significant item, so deducted here. Company has flagged further exposure (interest, superannuation, payroll tax) beyond the provision; that residual is carried in the bear scenario, not here.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-5.4% FY2022-26, -9.3% FY2023-26) diverges from revenue (+4.1%) by far more than 30%, but book equity is not a usable growth anchor for Woolworths: the FY2021 Endeavour demerger in-specie distribution, the A$2.0bn FY2022 off-market buyback, the A$1,492m FY2024 NZ Food goodwill impairment and a payout ratio above 100% of owner FCF each shrank equity for reasons unrelated to earning power. Revenue CAGR over the clean post-demerger window is used instead, cross-checked against underlying EBIT (+12.7% FY2026, roughly flat FY2023-FY2026 at A$3.0-3.1bn).
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs on the post-Endeavour window: '3yr' = FY2023->FY2026, '5yr' = FY2022->FY2026 (4 years; FY2021 is continuing-ops only and FY2020 includes Endeavour, so a true 5-year window is not like-for-like) except fcf_5yr_cagr which uses FY2021 continuing-ops owner FCF (A$974m) -> FY2026 as a 5-year span. eps_3yr_cagr is on underlying NPAT (A$1,618m FY2023 -> A$1,599m FY2026); statutory EPS is meaningless across this window (FY2022 includes the A$6.4bn Endeavour demerger gain, FY2024 the goodwill impairment). Owner FCF (OCF - capex - lease principal - SBC) 3-yr CAGR of 2.3% is below the reported-FCF CAGR of 4.0%: lease principal has grown 6-7%/yr (A$1,067m -> A$1,298m), faster than cash flow, so the reported figure flatters the trend. SBC is immaterial (0.12%) and is not the cause.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 4.5% off Q1 FY2027 Group sales +4.7% (Australian Food +6.9%) and H2 FY2026 Australian Food +5.7%, fading to the FY2022-26 revenue CAGR of ~4% and then to population-plus-inflation 2.5% as eCommerce penetration (15.9%) matures. NZ Food in AUD and BIG W held roughly flat inside the Group number.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC underlying EBITDA margin recovers from 8.63% (FY2026) toward 9.1%, i.e. back to and slightly above the FY2023-FY2024 underlying level of 8.85-8.9%, as the A$400m above-store cost program, Moorebank RDC productivity and higher-margin Cartology/Everyday Rewards mix offset wage inflation (~4% award rises) and ongoing price investment. Underlying EBIT growing faster than sales is management's standing medium-term aspiration; the base assumes it is only partly met because the Food and Grocery Code (1 July 2026) caps how much of the cost-out can be retained.

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2026 rebuild holds but does not accelerate. Australian Food keeps growing a touch above market on basket size, eCommerce and Everyday Rewards, Group sales grow 4.5% in FY2027 fading to 2.5% by FY2034. The A$400m cost program and the Moorebank RDC lift the pre-SBC underlying EBITDA margin from 8.6% to ~9.1% over five years - back to the FY2023-24 level plus a little mix benefit from Cartology - with the Food and Grocery Code and continued price investment preventing anything more. NZ Food stays subdued in AUD and BIG W stays marginally profitable. Capex normalises from 3.4% to 3.0% of sales as the supply-chain build rolls off. Lease cash grows slightly slower than sales. Owner FCF rises from ~A$1.3bn to ~A$2.3bn by FY2036 (1.8% -> 2.3% of sales); the 20x terminal cap binds (Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% is 20.5x). On this basis the stock at A$42 is pricing roughly 45x current owner FCF and ~32x underlying earnings, well above its own 22-28x history.
scenario_narratives.bull: The turnaround compounds. Australian Food sales momentum (Q1 FY2027 +6.9%) persists, eCommerce and On Demand keep taking share, Cartology retail media and PFD/Petstock deliver a third or more of EBIT growth each year, NZ Food reaches its double-digit return ambition and BIG W's profit holds. EBIT grows well ahead of sales as management aspires, taking the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 9.6% - above anything achieved post-demerger - and lease cost falls to 2.5% of sales on digital mix and fixed-rent leverage. Capex settles at 2.9%. The ACCC case and the Code prove manageable (fines, not structural remedies). Terminal growth 3.0% with the 20x cap still binding.
scenario_narratives.bear: The duopoly premium erodes. Aldi, Costco and Amazon take share; the Food and Grocery Code's excessive-pricing penalties and continued political scrutiny force price investment that is not recovered in cost-out; the ACCC discount-claims case ends in a material penalty and remediation grows beyond the A$850m provision (the company's own A$180-330m post-tax 'further exposure' range). Sales growth drops to 2-2.5% and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin compresses to 8.1% (below the FY2025 trough of 8.4%), lease cost delevers to 2.75% of sales on fixed rents, capex eases only to 3.1% (0.5pp above ex-ROU D&A) to defend the network. Owner FCF is ~A$0.9-1.0bn through the decade, barely covering the dividend, and a slower-growth retailer gets a 16x terminal cap at 2% growth.

probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is 0.12% of revenue, so house and street values sit within A$1.5/share of each other and band_position is degenerate (the price sits far above BOTH bases); SBC treatment is irrelevant to the gap between price and value here. Read band_position as not meaningful.
probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: Woolworths faces a live regulator on three fronts at once (ACCC litigation, a new Food and Grocery Code with pricing penalties, and an open payroll remediation whose provision rose from A$146m to A$850m in one year), while Aldi and Costco keep taking share in a thin-margin business - these are not tail events. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs NZ Food, BIG W, retail media and a benign Code outcome to land together, and the FY2026 margin recovery is one year old after a weak FY2025. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Woolworths is valued as an operating company on strict owner free cash flow: leases are treated as the operating rent they are (A$1.9bn/yr charged in the flows, lease liabilities excluded from net debt), SBC is expensed, significant items are excluded from the margin but the A$850m remediation provision is deducted in the bridge, and the flows are discounted at an AUD-built 7.5% WACC. The honest finding is that on this basis the business generates ~A$1.1-1.3bn of owner FCF against a A$52bn market capitalisation and has funded part of its dividend from borrowings since FY2023. The market at A$42 is paying for the FY2026 earnings recovery continuing at a pace the component build does not reproduce without margins exceeding anything achieved post-demerger.
key_risks_to_valuation: Lease treatment: charging full lease cash as an operating cost is the conservative but appropriate choice for a store network that is rented in perpetuity; a reader who prefers treatment (A) would add back ~A$1.9bn/yr of lease cash and deduct A$11.3bn of lease liabilities - the net effect on value is small but the terminal multiple optics change.
Capex vs D&A: the model carries capex 0.45pp of sales above ex-ROU D&A in perpetuity (growth capex); if Woolworths can hold capex at maintenance (~2.6%) the base IV rises by roughly A$4-5/share.

Regulatory: the Food and Grocery Code (1 July 2026) and the ACCC discount-claims case could compress margins below the bear path or impose structural remedies not modelled; the remediation provision could rise further.

WACC: at 7.5% the 20x terminal cap binds; at 7.0% the Gordon value (23x) would still be capped, so the valuation is relatively insensitive to small WACC moves but sensitive to the cap - see the sensitivity grid.
Working capital: negative WC releases cash with growth (3% capture); in a sales downturn this reverses, which the bear case only partly captures through a lower capture rate.
